questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Fines double in a work zone.

questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs with black markings alert drivers to road hazards. This sign warns you that bicycles may be crossing the road.

questions.question: Look ahead at least ______ seconds when riding your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Look at least 20 seconds ahead of your motorcycle. This gives you time to see hazards and react before you reach them.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes:

options.text: Involve riders with less than six months of experience.
Are caused by faulty ignition systems.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with less than six months of experience.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen to riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle. Be extra careful when riding a motorcycle that is new to you.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Keep riding. The wobble will likely stop on its own.
Slow down by closing the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down by closing the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not accelerate during a wobble—this makes it worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly, slow down by closing the throttle, lean your weight forward and down, and pull off the road safely. Then check what is causing the wobble.

questions.question: With a passenger, a motorcycle turns and changes direction:
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. The added weight makes your motorcycle slower to respond to turns and speed changes.

questions.question: In Wisconsin, who must wear a helmet?

options.text: Operators who have had a license for less than five years.

questions.explanation: Wisconsin law requires helmets for operators under 18 and anyone with a motorcycle instruction permit. All operators and passengers should wear helmets for safety.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A road joins from the right.
The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road will turn sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: Braking while turning is:

options.text: Easier than braking on a straight road.
Harder than braking on a straight road.
Safe with only the front brake.
Safe with only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than braking on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Braking while turning is more difficult than braking on a straight road. You can use both brakes, but you must know the right technique and be very careful.

questions.question: Your lane position should NOT:

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see better, stay out of blind spots, avoid hazards, and gives you an escape route. It should discourage other drivers from trying to share your lane.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should ride:

options.text: In the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can watch them from behind.

questions.question: When entering a curve, a group should:
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is usually best for groups. However, switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When it starts raining, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When it rains, do not ride in the center of the lane. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track often works best, but this depends on traffic and road conditions.

questions.question: When does alcohol impair your riding ability?
questions.explanation: Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol. Impairment begins well below the legal limit.

questions.question: When riding behind a car in the center of the lane:

options.text: Allows you to be seen in its rearview mirror.
Usually makes it difficult for the driver to see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows you to be seen in its rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When following a car, ride where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Usually, this means riding in the center of the lane. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so this position increases your visibility.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulation signs show rules that drivers must follow. This sign means parking is not allowed.

questions.question: What group formation should you use when riding?
questions.explanation: Usually, groups ride in staggered formation. Use single-file when taking curves, making turns, entering highways, or leaving highways.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn in the direction of the arrow. In this case, right turns are prohibited.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes:

options.text: Occur at speeds greater than 35 mph.
Involve riders who have little experience on their motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders who have little experience on their motorcycles.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes involve riders with little experience on their motorcycles.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This allows experienced riders to watch them from behind.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulation signs show rules that drivers must follow. This sign means stay on the right side to avoid a hazard ahead.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders:

options.text: Should wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
Should only wear hearing protection during long rides.
Should not wear hearing protection because it will block horns and sirens.
Do not need hearing protection if wearing a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can cause permanent hearing damage, even with a full-face helmet. Ear plugs protect your hearing while still letting you hear horns and sirens.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drive at a steady speed while looking and listening for trains.
Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, look both ways, listen for trains, and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with this sign, slow down and look both ways. Listen for trains and be prepared to stop. Never try to drive faster than an oncoming train.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to hazards or special situations ahead.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn your head, shoulders, and torso.

questions.explanation: Look through every turn by turning only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: To be effective, a face shield should not:
questions.explanation: A good face shield must be scratch-free, provide clear side views, fasten securely, and allow air to pass through. An airtight face shield causes fogging and makes it hard to see.

questions.question: If braking in a curve:

options.text: It is the same as braking on a straight road.
You have more traction as you lean into the curve.
You may have less traction as you lean into the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less traction as you lean into the curve.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but only with great care. The tires are already using some traction to turn while leaning, so less traction is available for braking.

questions.question: You will get the most protection from a helmet if it is all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: A helmet provides the best protection when it meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly all the way around, and has no defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must go straight ahead.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A road joins from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of an intersection ahead where a road joins from the right.

questions.question: Shifting gears in a curve:

options.text: Should only be done if it can be done smoothly.
Is better than shifting before the curve.
Is the best way to control your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should only be done if it can be done smoothly.
questions.explanation: It is best to shift gears before starting a turn. If you must shift while turning, shift smoothly. A sudden change in power to the rear wheel can cause a skid.
